name: Old Town
tagline: Stone houses around the Holy Trinity church, where the coworking is
description: Bansko's original village core of thick-walled stone houses and cobbled lanes around the Holy Trinity church and its bell tower. The mehanas are here, and so are the coworking spaces that built the town's nomad reputation. It is the most pleasant part to live in and the most social.
bestFor: Anyone here for the nomad community, with the coworking spaces on the doorstep
pros: Coworking spaces and the nomad social scene
Traditional mehanas and the best restaurants
Walkable to everything in the town
cons: Busy and noisy through the ski season
Old stone buildings vary in comfort

name: Gondola Base
tagline: Around the lift station, apartment blocks and ski-season noise
description: The strip near the gondola station where most of the construction-boom apartment blocks went up, aimed at the ski market. Out of season these sit half empty and rent for very little, which is exactly why the long-stay remote-work community found the town in the first place.
bestFor: Long stays taking advantage of empty ski apartments outside the season
pros: Very low rents from April to November
Gondola for skiing and summer hiking at the door
cons: Loud and expensive through the ski season
Ten to fifteen minutes from the old town

name: Pirin Street and the Centre
tagline: The main strip, apres-ski bars and the supermarkets
description: The commercial spine running from the town square towards the gondola, with the bars, the rental shops, the supermarkets and the taxi ranks. It is the loudest part of Bansko in winter and the most practical year-round, with everything you need for daily life on one street.
bestFor: Short winter stays that want the bars and the lifts both close
pros: All shops, supermarkets and services on one street
Halfway between the old town and the gondola
The centre of the apres-ski scene
cons: Traffic and taxi queues in season

name: Glazne River and the Northern Edge
tagline: Quiet residential streets along the river
description: The residential streets on the northern side of the town along the Glazne, with Bulgarian family houses, small guesthouses and a genuine local population that has nothing to do with skiing. Rents are low, the streets are quiet, and the town centre is a ten-minute walk.
bestFor: Longer stays that want quiet and a local street rather than the resort
pros: Genuinely quiet even in high season
Low rents and houses rather than blocks
Ten minutes on foot to the centre
cons: Little contact with the nomad community

name: Banya (5 km east)
tagline: The hot springs village down the valley
description: A small village five kilometres east with natural thermal springs and a row of small hotels and public baths built around them. It is quieter and cheaper than Bansko, has an outdoor pool culture that runs all winter, and is a ten-minute drive or a regular minibus from town.
bestFor: Stays that want the hot springs and are content to travel into Bansko
pros: Natural thermal baths and outdoor pools
Cheaper and much quieter than Bansko
Ten minutes by road to the town
cons: A car or the minibus is needed for everything
